subject: dependency-declaration
note: The constraint set here IS satisfiable - npm ci succeeds on Linux with a correct lock. The failure was that npm install on the maintainer's Windows box prunes platform-optional hoisted entries (@emnapi/core, @emnapi/runtime) out of the lock it writes. Three real cases: c0485d6 (the resolver refused and named the exact packages; under B there is no verdict to refuse with and the diagnosis moves one step later into a wasm-binding build error), c640015 (the team hand-authored the working set and wrote the reason at the install site, +10 lines in gates.yml - literally the technique's step 2, applied while keeping the resolver ON), and check-bundle.mjs's POSITIVE_CONTROL plus exit-2 (the technique's assert-the-instrument discipline, already deployed, against a satisfiable graph). Applying B would delete the only instrument that distinguishes a red-because-unsatisfiable from a red-because-the-lock-was-generated-on-the-wrong-host. Artifact: .ai/apply-2026-09-03/unsatisfiable-set.md.
return_condition: when this repo can name two mutually exclusive published upstream constraints - it currently cannot - the technique's precondition is met and the verdict should be retaken

subject: generated-output-grading
note: The tree already held the technique for ONE dimension and had independently written its reasoning: supportsReferences exists because a request field that is honoured by one adapter and silently dropped by another is a failure that looks like a success, so the router treats it as a routing constraint. negativePrompt has the identical property and had no declaration - leonardo.ts:142 sends a native negative_prompt field, google.ts:395 buildPrompt appends the exclusions to the positive prompt as a sentence competing with the subject for the same text budget. The two dimensions INVERT across the same provider pair (google typed on references, leonardo typed on negatives) and nobody designed that; it fell out of references being the one that visibly broke. Per the technique, the resolution here is declaration rather than routing - both vendors do honour it, so a routing constraint would wrongly ban google from negative-prompt work. Added negativePromptChannel to ImagingProvider and to Provenance (set only when the request carried one), stamped in the router so a forgetful adapter cannot reproduce the silent case. Paired against HEAD on one counter: unequal dimensions declared on the descriptor 1/2 -> 2/2, recorded on provenance 0/2 -> 1/2. tsc --noEmit clean. No vendor call was made, so the measurable is structural, not behavioural. Commit 65ea623.
return_condition: when Playground next runs a cross-provider grid with a negative prompt, read the recorded channel and check whether a flip attributed to the model survives at prose parity
